title: Functorial bounded-above flat replacement
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, with $\Lambda_T$ its constant sheaf of rings on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and flat module sheaves as in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. There is a construction which assigns to every bounded-above complex
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves together with an
integer $N$ such that $\mathcal F^i=0$ for $i>N$ a bounded-above
complex $\Phi(\mathcal F)^\bullet$ of flat $\Lambda_T$-module
sheaves with $\Phi(\mathcal F)^i=0$ for $i>N$ and a termwise
surjective quasi-isomorphism
$\Phi(\mathcal F)^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$; the construction is
functorial, in the sense that a map
$\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ between complexes which both
vanish above $N$ induces a map
$\Phi(\mathcal F)^\bullet\to\Phi(\mathcal G)^\bullet$ compatible with
the two quasi-isomorphisms. In particular every bounded-above complex
of $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-module sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ is quasi-isomorphic to a
bounded-above complex of flat sheaves. Here the last assertion holds for every integer $n$.

proof.text: Regard each $\mathcal F^i$ as a presheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$, by restricting its $\Lambda_T$-action along the constant-presheaf map $\Lambda\to\Lambda_T$. For any such presheaf $M$, define $B(M)(U)=\bigoplus_{s\in M(U)}\Lambda$. Write $[s]$ for its basis elements; restrictions send $[s]$ to $[s|_V]$, and a map $f:M\to M'$ sends $[s]$ to $[f(s)]$. Evaluation $e_M:B(M)\to M$, $[s]\mapsto s$, is sectionwise surjective and natural. On basis elements, identity and composition of maps are preserved, so $B$ is a functor (no additivity of this functor is asserted). All sums are sets in the chosen universe and can be formed after the small-skeleton convention. The constant sheaf is the sheafification of the constant presheaf.

source.place: Section 03CS (presheaves of modules); free-cover argument of 03EW (lemma-module-quotient-flat) made sectionwise and functorial

proof.text:
Construct a presheaf complex $C$ and an augmentation $q:C\to\mathcal F$. Put $C^i=0$ for $i>N$. Descend from $N$, with $Z^jC=\ker d_C^j$ and $Z^j\mathcal F=\ker d_{\mathcal F}^j$, using
$$P^i=\mathcal F^i\times_{Z^{i+1}\mathcal F}Z^{i+1}C,\qquad C^i=B(P^i).$$
The first map defining the fibre product is $d_{\mathcal F}^i$, which lands in cycles since $d_{\mathcal F}^{i+1}d_{\mathcal F}^i=0$; the second is the restriction of $q^{i+1}$ to cycles, available from the chain equations already constructed. Explicitly $P^i(U)$ consists of pairs $(x,z)$ with $d_{\mathcal F}x=qz$ and $d_Cz=0$. Define $q^i$ and $d_C^i$ by evaluation followed by the two projections, the latter followed by $Z^{i+1}C\hookrightarrow C^{i+1}$. Then $q^{i+1}d_C^i=d_{\mathcal F}^iq^i$ and $d_C^{i+1}d_C^i=0$ directly on each pair, so these really are complexes and a chain map. At $i=N$, the fibre product is $\mathcal F^N$, giving $C^N=B(\mathcal F^N)$. At each fixed degree there are only $N-i+1$ stages, so ordinary induction on this nonnegative integer defines every term.

Source error in the imported blueprint proof: its pullback uses the whole next term instead of its cycles, so it need not give a square-zero differential. On the one-point topos over $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, take $\mathcal F=\mathbf Z[0]$ and $N=0$. In its degree-zero free cover the nonzero basis vector $k=[0]$ has evaluation zero. Its degree-minus-one free cover contains $l=[k]$, with differential $k$. Its next full-term pullback contains $l$, so the degree-minus-two generator $[l]$ has second differential $k\ne0$. The cycle pullback used here excludes $l$ at that stage. This repairs the construction while retaining the statement and the free-cover/descending-resolution/sheafification route.

Prove simultaneously, sectionwise, that $q^i:C^i\to\mathcal F^i$ and $Z^iC\to Z^i\mathcal F$ are surjective. Above $N$ both claims hold between zero modules. Suppose the claims on cycles are known in degree $i+1$. Given $x\in\mathcal F^i(U)$, its differential is a cycle; choose $z\in Z^{i+1}C(U)$ with $qz=d_{\mathcal F}x$. The basis vector $[(x,z)]\in C^i(U)$ maps to $x$, proving the first claim. Given a cycle $x\in Z^i\mathcal F(U)$, the pair $(x,0)$ belongs to $P^i(U)$ and $[(x,0)]$ has differential zero and maps to $x$. This proves the second claim, completing the descending induction, including degree $N$. These arguments do not presume that an epimorphism of sheaves is surjective on sections: they concern the explicitly constructed presheaf free cover.

source.place: 05T7 (1), verification of the induction hypothesis, with explicit sectionwise lifts

proof.text: The map $q$ induces an isomorphism on cohomology at every section object $U$. Surjectivity follows from the cycle lift $[(x,0)]$ of step 3. For injectivity, let $c\in Z^iC(U)$ and suppose $q^i(c)=d_{\mathcal F}^{i-1}(a)$ for $a\in\mathcal F^{i-1}(U)$. Then $(a,c)\in P^{i-1}(U)$ and $b=[(a,c)]\in C^{i-1}(U)$ has $d_C^{i-1}b=c$, so $c$ is a boundary. This also covers degree $N$, and above $N$ both cohomologies vanish. By the statement on exact evaluation and sectionwise homology in [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], $q$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism of presheaf complexes.

Sheafify termwise, setting $\Phi(\mathcal F)^i=(C^i)^\#$. The exact module-sheafification result [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] sends the sectionwise epic maps $q^i$ to epimorphisms of sheaves and gives natural isomorphisms $H^i(C^\#)\cong H^i(C)^\#$; consequently $q^\#:C^\#\to\mathcal F$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Here the sheafification of the already sheaf-valued target is canonically the target itself, by the sheafification universal property. The same exactness sends zero terms to zero, retaining the upper bound $N$. The sheafified constant-presheaf ring is $\Lambda_T$, so these are $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves with the indicated augmentation. Explicitly, sheafify the scalar multiplication map of underlying presheaves of sets; preservation of finite products by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] identifies its domain with $\Lambda_T\times(C^i)^\#$. The module identities follow by sheafifying the identities for the original action. The differential and augmentation commute with this action because they do so before sheafification. On the already sheaf-valued target this action agrees with its given $\Lambda_T$-action: both extend the constant-presheaf action uniquely through sheafification. Thus the homology comparison and augmentation are $\Lambda_T$-linear. Kernels are computed on the underlying sheaves and cokernels are sheafified underlying quotients, with the induced actions, so the underlying cohomology isomorphisms give cohomology isomorphisms of $\Lambda_T$-modules.

Every $C^i(U)$ is a free $\Lambda$-module (or zero), hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Thus tensoring with $C^i(U)$ preserves exact sequences, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Presheaf evaluation is exact and computes kernels sectionwise, as stated in [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], so the objectwise tensor functor with $C^i$ preserves kernels. It preserves finite products as well: they are finite direct sums of modules, and the maps $m\otimes(a,b)\mapsto(m\otimes a,m\otimes b)$ and the sum of the two inclusions are mutually inverse. It sends zero to zero. Hence it preserves finite limits of presheaves. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat] with $\mathcal O$ the constant presheaf $\Lambda$ and $\mathcal F=C^i$: its sheafification is flat over $\mathcal O^\#=\Lambda_T$. This proves flatness of every term of $\Phi$ without assuming sectionwise flatness of an arbitrary sheaf.

source.place: 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves) and 03ET (lemma-flatness-sheafification); algebra.tex 00HD and the free-module observation in the proof of 051G

proof.text: For a chain map $f:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ with the same upper bound $N$, define the map between the constructed presheaf complexes by descending induction. It is the unique map between zero terms above $N$. If its component $h^{i+1}$ has already been constructed and respects cycles and augmentation, the map of pullbacks is $(x,z)\mapsto(f^i(x),h^{i+1}(z))$. The chain equations and $q_{\mathcal G}h=fq_{\mathcal F}$ show that the image satisfies both equations defining the target pullback. Apply $B$ to this map to obtain $h^i$. Evaluation naturality gives $d_{C\mathcal G}h^i=h^{i+1}d_{C\mathcal F}$ and $q_{\mathcal G}^ih^i=f^iq_{\mathcal F}^i$ on every basis vector. Identity and composition hold by induction on the two coordinates and on the free basis. Sheafification is a functor, so the resulting maps of $\Phi$ have the same equations and are functorial. Finally take $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ for the stated particular case; no invertibility, finiteness, or properness hypothesis is needed.
